wedge: public K-apt monthly apartment management-fee data + same-complex history + nearby/similar-complex benchmarks => consumer-facing anomaly watch that says what jumped, how unusual it is, and which cost category likely caused it, instead of making residents manually browse comparison tables
last_material_result: Fresh consumer data/alert discovery selected apartment maintenance-fee anomaly detection as the first survivor. K-apt already exposes rich management-fee lookup, 1:1 and 1:N comparisons, regional averages and monthly disclosure, so a generic comparison page has no wedge. However, the action-layer remains potentially distinct: recurring detection of a sharp month-over-month or peer-relative jump, plain-language cause breakdown, and a concise 'worth checking' signal. Public-data availability is strong and low-cost; the key risk is that official comparison functionality may already satisfy enough users that alert/action value is weak.
economics: KRW0 validation spend. Potential monetization: ads, household-services/energy affiliate or lead-gen, sponsorship, or premium alert history. Direct WTP is uncertain; this only works if recurring attention and organic/local search distribution are materially better than the official K-apt browse experience.
next_checkpoint: Next Lane C run: test three materially different wedges before any competition-based KILL: (1) monthly anomaly alert, (2) move-in due-diligence report comparing candidate apartments, (3) 'why did my fee jump?' category explainer using public benchmarks. Validate whether management-fee detail APIs are freely accessible enough for automated refresh without privileged/authenticated data.
recommendation: KEEP in ASSESS as first fresh survivor, but treat K-apt's strong official substitute as the primary disconfirming risk. Do not BUILD until action-layer and distribution gaps are evidenced.
